correctness.rationale: Commuting E and U=A-E equivalent to E in centralizer of A. Primary decomposition is canonical; for f=t nilpotent A forces ker E=0, and f=t-1 nilpotent A-I forces im E=0. Neutral factors make both A and A-I units on every direct summand so every centralizing idempotent is valid. For homogeneous blocks centralizer M_k(R), a finite chain ring with residue field F_Q, rank-r idempotents form GL_k(R)/(GL_r(R)xGL_(k-r)(R)); |GL_j(R)|=Q^((m-1)j^2)|GL_j(F_Q)|. This gives exponent (2m-1)r(k-r) exactly. Two valid choices on any neutral primary prove uniqueness criterion; condition A-A^2 nilpotent equivalent to only 0,1 primary factors. Independent direct local ring idempotent enumeration yields 26 in M2(F2[u]/u²) and 110 in M2(F3[u]/u²), matching H. Finite tests supplement, not replace proof.

value.rationale: A fixed matrix’s number of strongly clean decompositions is a natural exact invariant, and homogeneous primary blocks are canonical nonsemisimple rational-canonical strata. The formula quantifies effect of nilpotent thickness on a qualitative existence theory, with a sharp unrestricted elementwise uniqueness characterization. The necessary orbit-stabilizer algebra is elementary but the end-to-end exact formula covers arbitrary degrees, ranks and lengths and is practically usable without ad hoc enumeration.

final_claim: For each homogeneous f-primary module (F_q[t]/f^m)^k, neutral f other than t,t-1 contributes H_(m,k)(q^deg f)=sum_r GaussianBinomial(k,r,Q)*Q^((2m-1)r(k-r)) strongly clean decompositions; t and t-1 factors force E=I and E=0. For arbitrary A uniqueness iff A-A^2 is nilpotent.
limitations: Explicit H product only homogeneous primary modules; arbitrary matrix uniqueness criterion holds without homogeneity.
Originality under older module idempotent enumeration remains a residual risk.
